data.gender_notes: Barth is used as a male name in Christian naming traditions.
data.long_meaning: Derived from the Old German word 'berahta', meaning 'bright, shining, noble'. The name Barth is of Germanic origin and has been used primarily in the Christian tradition. The name Barth carries the meaning “Bright, noble” and is chosen by families in Christian traditions for the positive qualities it expresses. Linguistically it belongs to the Biblical tradition and is also used in English, Greek, Latin. Parents who choose Barth usually hope their child will grow to embody bright, noble and live with faith, good character and purpose.
data.spiritual_meaning: A shining beacon of faith and wisdom
data.etymology: Barth belongs to the Biblical linguistic tradition and is used in Christian naming. Its recorded meaning is “Bright, noble.”
data.numerology_meaning: In Pythagorean numerology the letters of Barth total 4, giving a life-path number of 4. Number 4 is linked with Rahu and with the qualities of stability, discipline and hard work.

in_greek.name: Βαρθ
in_greek.long_meaning: Τὸ ὄνομα Βαρθ προέρχεται ἐκ τῆς ἑβραϊκῆς γλώσσης καὶ σημαίνει παῖς τοῦ Ἀρὰμ, σύμφωνα πρὸς τὴν Γένεσιν ΚΗ ́3, ἔχον σημαντική θέση εἰς τὴν πρώιμην χριστιανικὴν παράδοσιν καὶ τὴν συνδέσει μὲ τὴν οἰκογένειαν καὶ τὴν γενεαλογίαν τοῦ Ἰησοῦ Χριστοῦ.

in_latin.name: Barth
in_latin.long_meaning: The name Barth originates from Hebrew, signifying son of Aram, as referenced in Genesis 28:3, holding considerable religious significance within early Christian tradition and culture, symbolizing lineage and familial bonds.

in_english.name: Barth
in_english.long_meaning: The name Barth is of Hebrew origin, meaning 'son of Aram' or 'farmer'. It is derived from the Hebrew name 'Bartholomew', which translates to 'son of Aram' or 'son of the earth'. In the New Testament, Bartholomew was one of Jesus' twelve apostles. The name holds significant spiritual meaning, symbolizing a connection to the earth and to family lineage. Throughout Christian tradition, Barth has been used as a given name, signifying strength, humility, and a connection to the land.

data.cultural_impact: Barth is a name synonymous with intellectual antecedents within the Protestant Christian tradition. Most notably, it is the surname of one of the 20th century's greatest theologians, Karl Barth. His groundbreaking work, "Dogmatics in Outline," has shaped theological thought and united the church with his assertion of the primacy of God's Word.
data.spiritual_significance: Carrying the name Barth instills a sense of responsibility to uphold the intellectual and spiritual heritage it represents. It speaks of a commitment to the search for truth, biblical exegesis, and a deep reverence for the divine nature of God. With the foundation laid by theologians like Barth, achieving a strong spiritual foundation and fostering a lifelong pursuit of knowledge become essential personal goals.
data.spiritual_symbolism: The name Barth carries profound spiritual symbolism as it is rooted in Biblical tradition. As a name associated with Saint Bartholomew, it represents holiness, devotion, and Christian virtue.
